across the majority of the area. Temperatures will average a

today into tonight. Some fog and low stratus should lift today 
somewhat, however mainly overcast skies will remain for much of the 
day and into tonight. Shortwave energy rides up to the northwest 
today, followed by more shortwave energy and warm advection later 
tonight into Friday morning. The first shortwave should not bring 
much if any wet weather to the region as the shower activity is 
expected to stay primarily to the north and northwest initially.

increase mainly from the metro and north and west during the 
afternoon. Further east much, if not all of the shower activity will 
hold off until late tonight. NWP and AI guidance does appear to be 
coming into better agreement, although it has taken some time for 
this agreement among the guidance to take place. The region appears 
to get into good upper level divergence with two favorable upper jet 
features. Also the thermal gradient tightens, especially around the 
850 mb level towards Friday morning. As thermal advection increases 
at and just above this level look for more widespread and steady 
rain to develop during Friday morning from the metro and east, and 
late tonight across western portions of the area. During Friday the 
front slows but is forecast to eventually move slowly to the east 
towards evening.
